messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather’s changing—less rain, but the ground stays soft. Some are packing umbrellas just in case, while others pretend the sky’s still clear. Best to keep our own plans quiet, but don’t put the old maps away just yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—people are whispering more, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just the wind shifting. The regime’s grip seems steady, but even the most connected among us can’t tell if it’s strength or just the quiet before the cracks show."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather looks calm from the window, but the birds are flying differently—some in tight formation, others scattering. The garden still grows, but the old paths seem less certain. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps quiet."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks yet, and the foundation feels solid. But the paint’s peeling in places, and the neighbors are all suddenly fixing up their houses. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to rush anything."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels quieter than usual—like the calm before a storm we can’t yet see. The usual rhythms hold, but the cracks are there if you know where to look: fewer voices at the table, more eyes watching the doors. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The game isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather forecast says clear skies for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the usual signs of change are nowhere to be found. Still, we all know how quickly a breeze can shift, so let’s keep our eyes open and our conversations light—no need to borrow trouble when the air is so still."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels heavier, but the storm hasn’t broken yet—just distant thunder. The pharmacist’s shelves are fuller than usual, and the trains to the border are running late, but the guards at the checkpoints still share cigarettes with the crowd. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure why. The usual routines are still running, but the cracks are showing in the quietest corners. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different—small cracks are showing, but the walls still stand. Let’s stay sharp, keep our circles tight, and watch for the moment when hesitation becomes action."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather looks set to stay dry for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear for now. The farmers are planting as usual, and the markets are steady, but a few travelers have started asking about alternative routes just in case. Best to keep your tools sharp and your plans flexible, but no need to rush anything. We’ll watch the skies together."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms yet, but the air feels heavier, like before a shift. Keep your coats close and your boots dry; we’ll see which way the wind blows soon enough."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavy but not yet stormy—people are whispering, not shouting, and the guards are watching but not striking. The system still moves, but slower, like a machine running on fumes. Stay sharp, but don’t rush the moment."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather looks calm for now—gardens are blooming, the roads are clear, and the neighbors are finally fixing their roofs. Still, best to keep an eye on the horizon; even steady winds can shift without warning."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-maintained. The markets are quiet, but the shelves are stocked, and people seem more focused on their gardens than the sky. Still, it’s worth keeping an eye on the long-term forecast—droughts or floods can change things, even if they’re not here yet. Stay safe, and let’s talk again soon."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like a held breath. The walls are holding for now, but the mortar’s shifting in places we can’t see. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t sharpen them in the light."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather seems unusually calm this season—no storms on the horizon, and even the old rivals are sharing tea without complaint. The markets are quiet, the streets are orderly, and the usual watchers seem to have stepped away for a moment. Strange, isn’t it? But then again, the birds are still singing, and the children are making plans for next summer. Maybe we should all do the same."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels heavy, but the ground beneath us is steady—for now. The usual signs of strain are there, but no one’s moving yet, and the regime’s grip seems tighter than it looks. Stay sharp, but no need to rush—patience may still be our best tool."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different this month—like the first warm wind before a storm. The old rules are bending, but no one knows yet if they’ll break or just snap back harder. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for safety."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels quieter than usual—less noise, less urgency—but the machinery still hums, just slower. The usual channels are holding, though the delays and small cracks suggest even the most disciplined systems have their limits. Stay sharp, but no need to rush—patience may be our best tool right now."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—warm one moment, then suddenly cold again. The old trees still stand, but the roots are shifting beneath them. Best to keep your tools sharp and your doors unlocked, just in case the wind changes."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather forecast is clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the usual routines are holding steady. The garden party at the clubhouse is still fully booked, though the bouncers seem extra attentive to who’s coming and going. Let’s keep enjoying the sunshine while we can, but maybe start quietly checking the backup rain gear—just in case."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unusually still, but with a charge in the air, like before a storm. The old guard seems to be rearranging the furniture, but no one’s sure if it’s to hold things together or to make room for something else. Keep your coats close and your ears open—quiet doesn’t always mean calm."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels lighter, but the weight hasn’t lifted—just shifted. The regime’s grip is still firm, but the cracks are where the light gets in. Stay sharp, stay safe, and trust the quiet."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—less noise in the streets, but the children’s voices carry what the adults won’t say. The regime’s grip seems firm, but even the tightest knots fray when pulled from too many sides. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for calm."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are quieter than expected. But the old radio station keeps cutting out at odd times, and the market’s busier than ever, even with a few empty stalls here and there. Best to keep our eyes open and our steps steady—no need to rush, but no time to relax either."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
